summary.headline: Manorama Q2 FY27 revenue rose 41.9% YoY to INR459 crore, with EBITDA margin at 25.8% and PAT up 51.8% to INR81 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR459 crore (up 41.9% YoY), with EBITDA of INR118 crore (up 34.4%) and PAT of INR81 crore (up 51.8%). H1 FY27 revenue reached INR863 crore (up 40.8%), with PAT of INR159 crore and net debt-to-equity down to 0.04x from 0.38x. Management attributed about 85% of YoY growth to volume and 10-15% to price realisation. Working capital absorbed cash: H1 operating cash outflow was INR252 crore, driven by inventory building to INR1,000 crore on early shea procurement. Leadership was reorganised, with Deep Saraf becoming Managing Director.

financial_highlights.value: INR25 crore (INR15 crore forex gain, INR10 crore FD interest)

segments.name: CBE and stearin (fractionation)
segments.commentary: Management said CBE and stearin contribute about 70-75% of value, up from 65-70% earlier; comfortable band of 70-80% with current capacity. Value-added products are about 75% of sales mix.

segments.name: Olein, refined butters and by-products
segments.commentary: Remaining roughly 25% of sales value, comprising olein, refined butters and by-products such as DOCs. No separate figures given.

guidance_outlook: No numeric revenue or EBITDA guidance; management expects healthy top-line growth for full FY27.
EBITDA margin band of about 25-27% described as comfortable; modest quarter-to-quarter movement possible.
Existing capacity (47,500 tpa) expected to run at 85-90% utilisation; 4,500 MTPA debottlenecking in planning for Q3 FY27, with the second-unit debottlenecking to be completed by end of FY27.

New capacities (Burkina Faso backward integration, fractionation, Latin America) expected to commission around Q3-Q4 FY28, with gradual contribution from FY29; new plants start at 40-50% utilisation and reach 85-90% in two to three years.
Africa sourcing expected to yield only 2-3% company-level cost benefit, per CFO.
Pricing benefit of 5-10% expected from inflation and other factors, per management.
Asset turn of about 6-7x on optimum utilisation, depending on product mix.
capex_capacity: Capex to date (including WIP) about INR70-75 crore, against a guided INR225-250 crore; management said the larger spend will come in H2 FY27 and FY28. An analyst cited a total programme of about INR460 crore.
4,500 MTPA debottlenecking under planning, with commercial production timing to be updated after the application is completed.
Burkina Faso backward integration: land acquired and regulatory approvals awaited; project timeline targeted at Q3-Q4 FY28.
Solvent fractionation plant in planning and engineering stage; no timeline given.
LATAM facility: already fully booked on existing capacity; volumes being shipped from India gradually, with ramp-up expected over the next few quarters to a year.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no demand slowdown or order deferral in export markets; capacities are booked for the next year.
Realisations rose 10-15% YoY, with the rest of growth from volume; management said CBE pricing is not directly linked to cocoa butter prices, and contract prices are stable.
Shea raw material cost rose mainly due to freight (Red Sea routing, fuel); management also cited 5-7% input inflation.
Receivables rose sharply vs March 2026, which management attributed to the last 15 days of September revenue; said normal average is about 30 days.
Exports are 61% of revenue, serving more than 39 countries.

qa_highlights.question: Is the rise in raw material cost versus the fall in other expenses a reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no change in reporting format; the increase reflects higher freight and transport costs in gross margin, linked to Red Sea and fuel price movements.

qa_highlights.question: Volume versus price split of the 42% revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: About 85% from volume and 10-15% from price realisation, per Ekta Soni.

qa_highlights.question: Why was inventory built up and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Early shea procurement from West Africa, plus seasonal sal and mango buying; management said inventory should normalise in Q3 and Q4, though it could not confirm that seasonality will be confined to H1.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin improve as new capacity comes on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are in the 25-27% band and operating leverage and mix should help gradually, but gave no numeric targets.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a slowdown in exports due to geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management said products are short in supply and demand is healthy.

qa_highlights.question: Shea price versus freight contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight is the main driver; there may also be 5-7% input inflation. The exact freight increase percentage was not disclosed and will be provided offline.

risks_watch: Working capital: inventory of INR1,000 crore and H1 operating cash outflow of INR252 crore; watch normalisation in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Capex execution: only about INR70-75 crore spent against a guided INR225-250 crore; large spend and commissioning are pushed to H2 FY27 and FY28.
Freight and logistics costs (Red Sea, fuel) pressuring gross margin; freight increase percentage not disclosed.
Management transition: new MD and reorganised leadership; first call as MD.
Limited disclosure on capacity addition and growth levers; several questions deferred offline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and H1 results, but evasive on capex progress, freight cost quantum, growth drivers beyond FY27 and new capacity figures, often deferring to earlier disclosures or offline follow-up.
key_quotes: Our quarterly revenue is now above INR400 crores.

This inventory is raw material, and its stock will be converted and sold, as we expect to normalize through the second half working capital is funded through our existing banking limits and internal resources.
Comparing 40%, 30%, or 50% would not be the right thing to do.

adds.what: 4,500 MTPA debottlenecking of existing plant (under planning, application pending)
Burkina Faso backward integration (land acquired, approvals awaited)
Solvent fractionation plant (planning and engineering stage, no timeline)

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects healthy top-line growth for FY27, backed by existing capacity at 85-90% utilisation, export bookings for the next year, a 5-10% pricing benefit and a 4,500 MTPA debottleneck in planning for Q3 FY27, while new capacity (Burkina Faso, fractionation, LATAM) only commissions around Q3-Q4 FY28.

mgmt.note: Deep Saraf became Managing Director in a leadership reorganisation; the brief gives no stated growth plan from him.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin at 25.8% in Q2 FY27 sits in a 25-27% comfortable band, with management saying operating leverage and mix should help gradually but giving no numeric target; freight costs (Red Sea, fuel) and 5-7% input inflation are headwinds.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Existing 47,500 tpa running at about 85% utilisation, with a 4,500 MTPA debottleneck in planning for Q3 FY27 (about 9.5% of capacity) and Burkina Faso, fractionation and LATAM only commissioning around Q3-Q4 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: About 85% of the 41.9% Q2 revenue growth came from volume, export capacities are booked for the next year, and the company says there is no demand slowdown; utilisation is capped at 85-90% until debottlenecking lands.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 85%, with capex at only INR70-75 crore against a guided INR225-250 crore and a larger spend pushed to H2 FY27 and FY28, so further capex disclosures are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numeric guidance was given; management expects healthy FY27 top-line growth and H1 revenue was up 40.8%, but the outlook stays qualitative.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex is running well behind plan (INR70-75 crore spent against INR225-250 crore), freight costs are pressuring gross margin, and the freight increase has not been quantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was discussed; the growth story rests on existing CBE, stearin and olein lines plus capacity additions.

rows.label: Inventory normalisation after H1 build
rows.why: Inventory rose to INR1,000 crore from INR728 crore (March 2026) and H1 operating cash outflow was INR252 crore; management expects normalisation in Q3-Q4 but could not confirm it.

rows.label: LATAM facility ramp-up
rows.why: The LATAM facility is fully booked on existing capacity and volumes are shipping from India, with ramp-up expected over the next few quarters to a year.

rows.label: Africa sourcing cost benefit
rows.why: The CFO sized the Africa sourcing benefit at only 2-3% of company-level cost, so it is not a material margin lever.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, export bookings and the H1 margin band, but cautious and evasive on capex progress, the freight cost quantum and new capacity figures, often deferring to offline follow-up; analysts pressed on the volume/price split, inventory build and freight costs.

oneOffs.what: INR15 cr forex gain within H1 other income of INR25 cr (H1 revenue not affected; Q2-specific amount not separated)
Receivables jumped vs March, attributed to last 15 days of September revenue; possible late-quarter revenue loading, not quantified

quality.why: Q2 revenue growth of 41.9% is about 85% volume and 10-15% price, with no acquisitions and no growth-excluding-item disclosed, so the core is recurring; however the brief flags a INR15 cr H1 forex gain (inside other income, which flatters PAT) and a sharp receivables rise tied to the last 15 days of September, which may partly pull revenue into the quarter, and neither is quantified for Q2 alone.
